Subject: Increased tail latency / throughput drop on our dedicated pool

Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Throughput regression observed on dedicated GPU pool - preliminary findings

Quick technical update — short version up front: autoscaler decision latency appears to be the root trigger.

Findings: 
- Metrics ingestion pipeline (prometheus -> aggregator) experienced a ~90s ingestion lag between 15:10–16:10 PT on 2026-11-13, causing the autoscaler to make scale-down decisions based on stale lower utilization.
- Several nodes in dpool-stel-01 entered a transient degraded state (elevated GPU memory pressure) concurrent with the lag, worsening queuing behavior.
- No kernel panics or hardware faults detected.

Mitigation performed (Nov 14 09:00 UTC):
- Fixed metrics collector restart and patched backpressure guard in the autoscaler to ignore stale samples older than 60s.
- Rebalanced pods on the pool and cleared KV caches that were contributing to memory pressure.
- We validated throughput returned to expected baselines for a controlled subset and began rolling the fix to the rest of the pool.

Next steps: finalize RCA draft and share a recovery timeline with the customer. We should also recommend longer-term telemetry filtering and an alert to prevent similar stale-sample scale decisions.

Attachment: rca-draft.pdf (PDF)

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Recovery confirmation and post-incident plan for Nov 13 throughput regression

Hi Raj — following up with the recovery summary and next steps. Thank you for your patience while we investigated.

Summary / timeline (concise):
- 2026-11-13 15:10 PT: metric ingestion lag begins; autoscaler decisions use stale lower-utilization samples.
- 2026-11-13 15:20 PT: customer sees p99 increase and throughput drop (~40%) on dpool-stel-01.
- 2026-11-13 17:00 PT: we enabled a partial fallback (20% to rwd-small-v1) to reduce user impact.
- 2026-11-14 09:00 UTC: autoscaler patch deployed and impacted nodes rebalanced; throughput returned to baseline during controlled validation.

What we did for Stellara:
- Immediate mitigation: partial fallback routing and KV cache clears.
- Compensation: preliminary 25% service credit for the affected window; our finance team will send a formal credit note.
- Short-term fix: autoscaler backpressure guard to ignore samples older than 60s (deployed).
- Long-term actions: improve telemetry health alerts, add an explicit stale-sample alarm to prevent similar erroneous scale decisions, and run a targeted load test on dpool-stel-01 with your traffic profile.

We’ve drafted a concise RCA and uploaded it here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRCAPM-stellara-rca. The public postmortem will be published to this link once the doc is finalized: https://app.redwood.com/postmortem/STEL-4321.

As a next step, Marissa will reach out and propose a 1:1 ops session this week to walk through the RCA and the load test plan. We’ll also set up two weeks of elevated monitoring for Stellara at no extra cost.

Please let me know if you’d like additional details or a scheduled call — we can be available today.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll follow up with the finalized RCA and the formal credit note shortly.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
